2_motivation:
F22 (`modes_cap = 12` never scales with resolution — 12 of 128 modes at
256²) with candidate M1's proposed 32, measured on the certified champion
`mf_fno_transfer_film`. This is the card program.md §12.5 pre-directs
(*"G4's dry-run card (`s5_tuning-B1`, modes_cap 12→32 on the champion) is a REAL
batch-1 card for this stream."*) and the one `state/gates.md` G4 is PENDING on. The
websearcher's prior-art verdict licenses it as a **measurement, not a novelty claim**:
*"`modes_cap` 12 -> 32 is therefore a measurement of this project's own spectral
bottleneck (F22), not a mechanism contribution — which is exactly what a `tuning`-class
card should be, and it stays inside §12.5 (a hyperparameter, not a new
mechanism/architecture)."* Four streams currently reason under the unexamined
assumption that a 9.4%-of-Nyquist truncation is part of why fusion loses to copy-LF;
one 3-seed run confirms or removes that assumption for all of them.

prior_art.verdict_quote:
**PRIOR-ART VERDICT: not novel, and must not be claimed as such — but legitimate as a
measurement.** The mode-count question is published prior art: **iFNO**
(https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.15188, verified first-hand this run) grows K during
training and gets **10% lower error with 20% FEWER modes**; **AFNO** sparsifies modes;
**MG-TFNO** factorizes them. `modes_cap` 12 -> 32 is therefore a *measurement of this
project's own spectral bottleneck* (F22), not a mechanism contribution — which is
exactly what a `tuning`-class card should be, and it stays inside §12.5 (a
hyperparameter, not a new mechanism/architecture).

All comparisons are PAIRED against the ADR-0005 same-hardware cap-12 control (recert/training_h100/mf_fno_transfer_film), whose test predictions were regenerated by re-running THIS card's family entrypoint with MFFP_MODES_CAP=12 on the recert last.pt (eval-only branch). Seam-checked against the official recert JSONs on the round's metric (per-sample-mean rel-L2, score_panel.py:154): rel delta 7.8e-06 (helmholtz), 6.5e-05 (ifc_poisson), 3.5e-05 (phase_field_crystal), 2.1e-05 (allen_cahn), 3.2e-05 (cahn_hilliard, 24-sample subset), 9.2e-03 (fisher_kpp, 24-sample subset - see surprises). No card score is taken from a regenerated run; the official JSONs remain the source of truth. Turn files: <worktree>/scratchpad/reanalysis_turn_{1,2,3}_results.md.
findings: ext__helmholtz_2d, the dataset carrying 100% of the panel movement: the cap-32 gain is entirely AMPLITUDE and tail. Per-sample optimal rescale leaves cap 32 at 0.8980 vs cap 12 at 0.8166 - at matched amplitude cap 32 is 10% WORSE. alpha_mean 0.0710 (cap 32) / 0.0484 (cap 12): both arms over-predict amplitude ~14-21x. With a single global alpha both collapse to the predict-zero line (1.009 / 1.153) while copy-LF is 0.503. [turn 1, turn1_helmholtz_decomposition.json, turn1_ext__helmholtz_2d_tail.json]

ext__helmholtz_2d is a tail effect, not a typical-sample effect: only 66% of the 100 test samples improve; the 5 worst supply 43% of the mean gap and the worst 20 supply 86%; worst-sample rel-L2 falls 50.20 -> 8.91, p90 16.01 -> 5.81; trimmed means converge (best-50% 1.882 -> 1.601). 99% (cap 32) / 95% (cap 12) of samples are worse than predicting zero. [turn 1]
The two arms' helmholtz predictions are mutually uncorrelated: mean per-sample corr(pred_cap32, pred_cap12) = 0.018 (median -0.040). [turn 1]

ifc_poisson, the one dataset where the model works (per-sample corr with HF = 0.9942 / 0.9937; 8.5x better than the HF-train-mean field 0.4034 or nearest-in-X-train 0.3994): NO overfitting at N_hf=5 with 7.04x more spectral parameters. Train nRMSE (5 HF samples) 0.020329 -> 0.018031 (-11.3%), test 0.055627 -> 0.047479 (-14.6%); the fit gap NARROWED (2.736 -> 2.633). Test improved more than train. [turn 2, turn2_fitgap.json]

ifc_poisson is where modes_cap acts as a genuine BANDWIDTH knob: relative band error falls only at and above the cap-12 truncation edge k=12 - band [8,16) 0.3082 -> 0.2679, band [16,32] 0.3359 -> 0.2660, band [4,8) (inside both bandwidths) unchanged 0.2352 -> 0.2348 - and the cap-12 energy DEFICIT above k=16 (0.771 of HF energy) is more than halved (0.899). Amplitude share of error is only 0.098/0.040 there (alpha ~ 0.996), so the gain survives amplitude removal (0.0534 -> 0.0428). [turn 2]

All four sharp-2D datasets: cap 32 injects MORE spurious high-wavenumber energy than cap 12. E_pred/E_HF in the top radial band: phase_field_crystal 2.38e12 -> 2.15e13 (9.05x), allen_cahn 2.02e8 -> 6.96e8 (3.45x), cahn_hilliard 9.26e4 -> 1.58e5 (1.71x, n=24), fisher_kpp 8.55 -> 161.5 (18.90x, n=24); second-from-top band 1.88x, 1.89x, 7.07x, 6.20x. The HF fields hold >99.9% of their energy in the lowest band. [turn 3, turn3_summary.json, turn3_spurious_energy.png]

The sharp regression is not amplitude: after per-sample optimal rescale cap 32 remains worse on 3 of 4 (allen_cahn 0.26133 -> 0.26225, cahn_hilliard 0.43944 -> 0.45854, fisher_kpp 0.25173 -> 0.27429); only phase_field_crystal reverses (0.41983 -> 0.41803). [turn 3]

DECISIVE CONTROL - on 3 of the 4 sharp datasets and on helmholtz the champion's field prediction carries essentially NO pattern information; its whole apparent skill is the DC (spatial-mean) term. Per-sample correlation of the spatially DEMEANED fields: allen_cahn 0.0108/0.0118, phase_field_crystal 0.0074/0.0110, fisher_kpp 0.0017/0.0029, helmholtz 0.1272/0.0362 - against copy-LF 0.973-0.998 and ifc_poisson 0.994. On allen_cahn the HF DC energy share is 0.981, the predicted spatial mean is right to 4.4-4.7%, and the pattern-only nRMSE is 1.013/1.018, i.e. exactly the value of predicting zero pattern. [turn 3, turn3_dc_pattern_split.json]

The champion is WORSE than the constant-field oracle (each test sample's own spatial mean) on three panel datasets: allen_cahn 0.2648/0.2635 vs oracle 0.2591, phase_field_crystal 0.5208/0.5134 vs 0.3491, helmholtz 2.9508/6.4680 vs 0.8536. [turn 3]
interpretation: MECHANISM (high confidence, directly measured): modes_cap is not one knob but two, and which one it is depends on whether the condition-vector-to-field map is learnable on that dataset. Where it is learnable (ifc_poisson, corr 0.994) modes_cap is a true SPECTRAL BANDWIDTH knob and F22 is real: cap 12 systematically under-produced energy above k~12 and cap 32 fills it, worth 14.6% nRMSE / 0.247 skill units. Where it is not (the four sharp-2D sets and helmholtz, corr 0.001-0.13) the model is a DC predictor plus an uncorrelated noise pattern, and modes_cap merely sets how many spectral channels that noise may occupy - so raising it strictly adds spurious high-k energy and the score degrades.

WHY THE MAP IS NOT LEARNABLE (high confidence; imported measurement from s2_beyond_copy-B1 M1, same family, same checkpoints): the champion mf_fno_transfer_film is LF-BLIND at inference - the only tensor entering the network is the [batch, cond_dim] condition vector, zero field-shaped inputs. Its multi-fidelity mechanism is transfer learning in the WEIGHTS, not fusion at inference. A bandwidth knob on a decoder that never sees the LF field cannot recover interface structure it was never shown; s2's finding that a 1-NN-in-X lookup beats the champion on 4 of 5 sharp datasets is the same fact from the input side.

WHY HELMHOLTZ MOVED -4.861 WITHOUT ANY LEARNING GAIN (high confidence): on a broken predictor the reported nRMSE is dominated by the right tail of the per-sample amplitude blow-up. Extra decoder capacity compresses that tail (worst sample 50.2 -> 8.9) and pulls the mean scale error down (alpha 0.048 -> 0.071) while the shape gets slightly worse. This is exactly the phenomenon the certified 9.695 helmholtz min_claimable_effect encodes across seeds; the initial analyzer's refusal of a numeric claim there is mechanistically correct, not merely conservative.

WHY NO OVERFITTING AT N_hf = 5 (medium confidence, hypothesis H-PRETRAIN): the effective sample count for the spectral weights is not 5 but ~100 - the LF pretrain stage trains the same network on 100 LF fields for the full 200 epochs and the HF stage only fine-tunes at lr 3e-4 with cosine decay. The card conflated parameter count with effective sample count for a two-stage transfer recipe. A direct test needs a pretrain-stage checkpoint, which neither arm saved.

CONSEQUENCE FOR FOUR STREAMS (high confidence): the assumption that a 9.4%-of-Nyquist truncation is part of why fusion loses to copy-LF is now measured and removed for the sharp panel. Spectral bandwidth is a real but small lever exactly where the model already works, and a mild NEGATIVE lever where it does not. Capacity is not the bottleneck; the absence of a field-conditioned input path is.

SCOPE CAVEAT: cap 32 is full Nyquist on ifc_poisson (64x64), 67% on helmholtz (96x96), 50% on phase_field_crystal (128x128) and only 25% on the three 256x256 sets. The sharp-panel result therefore bounds the bandwidth hypothesis at 25% of Nyquist, not at Nyquist - but since the failure there is a missing pattern signal rather than a truncated one, going further up is measurably counterproductive (F11).
6_analysis.falsification_postmortem: The clause (geomean improvement >= 0.884 OR any stable dataset beyond its floor) landed 'not_resolvable' at the numbers, and the mechanism explains why it had to. Only one panel dataset (ifc_poisson) is in the regime where modes_cap can act as bandwidth at all, and the total effect available there is ~0.25 skill units against a 0.240 floor - a 4% margin, i.e. the experiment was underpowered by construction on the panel it was scored on. On the other five datasets the clause was testing a knob against a model whose field prediction carries no pattern information (demeaned corr 0.001-0.13), where more modes can only add uncorrelated energy; those five contributed movements of +0.06 to +0.29 skill (wrong direction) plus one 4.861-unit tail artefact on helmholtz that the noise floor already declares unclaimable. The scientific content of the card is therefore NOT the geomean but the regime split it exposed: F22 is real and small where the model works, and inverted where it does not. The card's own per-dataset prediction for ifc_poisson ('worse - full 64^2 spectrum from N_hf=5') is falsified in direction, and the reason is identified: two-stage transfer makes the effective sample count for the spectral weights the LF count (100), not the HF count (5).
surprises: The champion's predictions on 3 of the 4 sharp panel datasets are uncorrelated with the truth once the spatial mean is removed (|corr| <= 0.012) yet score nRMSE 0.26-0.52, because 63-98% of the HF field energy sits in the DC term. Every skill number on those datasets is a measurement of how well a conditional-mean predictor guesses one scalar per sample.
The champion is worse than the constant-field oracle (predict each sample's own spatial mean) on allen_cahn, phase_field_crystal and helmholtz.
Two runs of the same recipe differing only in modes_cap produce helmholtz predictions that are mutually uncorrelated (mean per-sample corr 0.018).
ifc_poisson's improvement came with a NARROWER train/test gap - 7x more parameters on 5 HF samples improved test more than train.

sharp__fisher_kpp_2d is the only dataset whose cap-12 checkpoint does not reproduce its official recert score to float noise on CPU: a systematic +0.3..+3.3% per-sample bias on all 24 subset samples (rel delta 9.2e-03 vs <= 6.5e-05 elsewhere), most consistent with H100 reduced-precision matmul in the spectral einsum. Worth a one-line check by whoever next compares CPU-side reproductions of GPU checkpoints.

Infrastructure: the login node (nproc=1, load average ~20 from concurrent agents) could not complete a 100-sample 256^2 cap-12 forward pass inside the 20-minute analysis cap, twice. The two 256^2 datasets were probed on a 24-sample paired subset instead.

7_gap_and_future.open_question: The champion's field prediction on 3 of the 4 sharp panel datasets is a DC (spatial-mean) level plus an uncorrelated noise pattern (demeaned corr 0.001-0.012, pattern-only nRMSE ~1.0). Is that because the condition vector genuinely does not determine the field at these sample counts, or because the two-stage transfer recipe destroys the pattern it learned during LF pretraining? The recipe re-normalizes between stages (a single global max|y| scaler per stage, scaler_lf -> scaler_hf) and then fine-tunes 200 epochs on 400 (sharp) or 5 (poisson) HF samples at lr 3e-4. s2-B1 shows a 1-NN-in-X lookup BEATS the champion on 4 of 5 sharp datasets, which means the X->field map carries more information than the trained model extracts - so the pattern collapse is at least partly a training/normalization artefact, not an information limit. Nobody has measured the LF-pretrain-stage checkpoint's test skill; that single number decides it.
7_gap_and_future.next_direction: For s5_tuning batch 2, per program.md 12.5 (knobs on existing recipes only), the leading candidate is the NORMALIZATION knob, not another capacity knob. Grounds: (a) the champion's helmholtz error is 70-87% pure amplitude with alpha ~ 0.05-0.07 (predictions 14-21x too large) and s2-B1 independently measured 86.5% amplitude share there; (b) the family uses ONE global scalar per stage, `scaler = max(|Y_stage|)`, which is set by the single most extreme training field and is re-derived between the LF and HF stages, so the network's output scale is re-anchored at fine-tune time; (c) unlike modes_cap, this knob acts on the failure mode that is actually dominant, and it is a pure hyperparameter (no new loss, no architecture change). Concrete arm: per-sample (or robust-quantile, e.g. 99.5th percentile) output normalization with the scale predicted from the condition vector, plus a stage-consistent scaler, measured against the same paired same-hardware cap-12 control. Falsification must clear 0.884 on the geomean and the per-dataset floors; note in advance that ext__helmholtz_2d (floor 9.695) cannot carry the verdict. SECONDARY (cheaper, diagnostic-class): a LEVEL-vs-PATTERN ablation - report every panel number alongside `tools/dc_pattern_split.py`'s constant-field oracle, so future cards cannot bank a DC-only score as fusion skill. NOT RECOMMENDED as batch 2: the operator's held modes+muP-LR conditional branch. Turn 3 shows the extra modes are filled with uncorrelated energy on 5 of 6 panel datasets, so re-tuning the LR for those modes optimises a knob whose measured sign is negative there; if it is run anyway it should be scoped to ifc_poisson, the one dataset in the bandwidth regime, where cap 32 already bought 14.6% nRMSE and muP-LR might convert the remaining k>12 deficit (E_pred/E_HF still 0.899 vs 1.0) into the ~0.25 skill units needed to clear the paper bar.
7_gap_and_future.cross_stream_notes: 1) F22 IS ANSWERED FOR THE WHOLE ROUND: modes_cap 12 was a real truncation only where the model already predicts a pattern (ifc_poisson, 64x64, worth 14.6% nRMSE); on the sharp-2D panel raising it is mildly NEGATIVE (1.7-18.9x more spurious top-band energy, all four datasets worse). No stream should carry 'the 9.4%-of-Nyquist wall' as an open assumption any more. 2) FOR s2_beyond_copy: your LF-blindness result, seen from the output side - on sharp__allen_cahn_2d, sharp__phase_field_crystal_2d and sharp__fisher_kpp_2d the champion's demeaned prediction is uncorrelated with the truth (|r| <= 0.012) and its pattern-only error equals predicting zero pattern; it is WORSE than the constant-field oracle on allen_cahn, phase_field_crystal and helmholtz. The honest framing is 'the model never had a field input and defaults to a conditional mean', not 'the model blurs the interface'. 3) FOR s6_local, s3_warp, s4_hybrid_routing: do not spend a batch on capacity, bandwidth or resolution. Whatever you add (local branch, warp field, expert routing) is meaningless unless the LF FIELD enters the forward pass at inference - check that first with tools/lf_at_inference_audit.py, and check the result with tools/dc_pattern_split.py. 4) FOR s7_loss: rel-L2 on these datasets is largely a level-regression metric (HF DC energy share 0.63-0.98); an interface-aware objective should be validated on the demeaned field, or it will be scored mostly on a scalar it does not touch. 5) OPERATIONAL: the round's metric is splits.<split>.rel_l2_mean (per-sample mean, score_panel.py:154), NOT the family JSON's legacy ratio-of-sums `nRMSE` field - they differ by 3x on ext__helmholtz_2d. 6) OPERATIONAL: control runs that ship only last.pt can be turned into paired predictions after the fact with tools/regen_preds_from_ckpt.py; no retraining, seam-checked to <= 6.5e-05 on five of six panel datasets.
